label: D2: rare a1->S2 transition (reached S2 after choosing a1)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (never D1/GO), and almost only when the reached-state input is S2 (100% of mass). Conjoined with the last-action input a1, i.e. a rare transition a1->S2, it gives dev P=0.75 R=0.85 F1=0.80, mass recall 0.93; top quartile coverage ~100%. Uses only inputs observed at D2 (equivalently common==0 & state==2). Misses (6.5% of mass) are weak firings on common a2->S2 transitions. False positives are concentrated late in the episode: firing rate declines steadily with ep_trial (6.7% of steps in trials 0-9 vs 0.2% in 90-99); adding ep_trial<80 raises dev F1 to 0.84 but I recorded the simpler input-only predicate. Does not fire on S1 at all, nor on rare a2->S1 transitions, so it is specific to the a1->S2 rare transition rather than rareness in general.

issues: The core facts hold. The unit is active only at D2 (D1 and GO have 0 active steps). S1 is almost never active (552 of 183,887 in_state==1 steps). The predicate scores dev F1 0.799 and test P 0.752 / R 0.827 / F1 0.787 / mass recall 0.922. The misses are weak firings on a2->S2 common steps (in_action==2 & in_state==2 has 13.5% of active steps but 6.5% of the mass).
The verdict overclaims. Test F1 is 0.787, below the 0.8 bar for 'explained', yet the agent recorded EXPLAINED.

The false positives form a systematic class, not noise. Inside the predicate, precision falls steeply with ep_trial: 0.996 at ep_trial<10 and 0.355 at ep_trial>=70. The firing rate in trials 90-99 is 0.002. Late firings are also weak: for ep_trial>=70 the predicate covers 0.0 of the top activation quartile. So the gap is not only in firing rate; magnitude falls as well. The label, 'D2: rare a1->S2 transition', leaves out that the unit goes silent on exactly this transition late in the episode.

There is a second systematic modulation from the previous reward. Inside the predicate, precision is 0.895 when prev_reward==0 and 0.681 when prev_reward==1. Most of the top-quartile mass is in prev_reward==0 (coverage 0.70 vs 0.30). The explanation does not mention this.

Smaller asymmetries that are not mentioned: precision is 0.85 with start_high==1 vs 0.64 with start_high==0. The predicate also fires mostly while S1 is good (77% of the mass), but that follows from a1 being chosen more often then; precision is similar either way (0.75 vs 0.77).

Better predicates on the test split: adding ep_trial<80 gives F1 0.828 (P 0.882, R 0.781, mass recall 0.899). Adding ((ep_trial<80) | (prev_reward==0)) gives F1 0.833 (P 0.851, R 0.815, mass recall 0.919). Neither uses a future variable. ep_trial is not a direct input, but the GRU can track elapsed time, and prev_reward is the D1 input it has already seen.
